newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UCB says it knows of no takeover plans.
newsitem.headline: UCB says it knows of no takeover plans.

text.p: Belgian drugs, fine chemicals and plastic films group UCB said the recent strong rise in its share price on the Brussels bourse was "strange indeed."
Chief executive officer Georges Jacobs told Reuters after the presentation of first half 1997 results that, to his knowledge, UCB was not being taken over.
"It is strange indeed to see the value of your share multiply by three," Jacobs said, noting that 20 years ago the shares had been worth 800 francs each.
The stock began to take off sharply at the end of May, when it was at 95,600 francs, peaking at 153,000 on July 17. It closed at 139,250 francs on Wednesday.
Analysts have said the share was overvalued at current levels, rating it at best a 'hold'.
Jacobs noted the share was illiquid. "The market is limited, making it easier to make an impact."
He noted investors were looking for growth and return and UCB had been following a strategy aimed at offering both.
At the time of the rally in UCB shares market talk centred on a London broker acting on behalf of an aggressive buyer ready to pay whatever it took for UCB.
But there were takeover rumours too.

Belgian bulk chemicals maker Solvay, which has its eye on expanding more aggressvely into pharmaceuticals, was named as well as Johnson & Johnson and Pfizer, both of the U.S. Solvay denied the rumours, branding the story an old chestnut.
As UCB's marketing partner in the U.S. for the Belgian company's star anti-allergy drug Zyrtec, Pfizer has a link to UCB. There is no known connection between UCB and Johnson.
Jacobs noted there was a stable core of UCB shareholders holding 36 percent. The company also had a poison pill structure in place since 1988, enabling it to draw up a defensive shield quickly.
"If there was a hostile threat, (core shareholders) would have over 50 percent together in two hours' time," he said.
